newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosnia trip causes anguish for German Greens.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia trip causes anguish for German Greens.

text.p: A fact-finding trip to Bosnia by members of Germany's opposition Greens party reopened old wounds on Tuesday over whether Bonn should offer troops for the international peace force (IFOR) if its mandate is renewed.

While the party's hardline pacifists argued Germany's World War Two Nazi past meant it should avoid foreign intervention, the pragmatists said it was time to realise all sides in the Bosnian conflict wanted the German army to stay.
"A protective shield is necessary to prevent Bosnia from being divided and that shield can only be a military one," the party's co-leader Krista Sager told reporters.
"Germany plays an important role in Europe and it can't delegate that role to anyone else."

But the split in the party, which hopes to complete a transition from a bastion of radical student politics to respectable coalition partner, was underscored when Sager's co-leader Juergen Trittin took a very different view.

"The success of IFOR's successor has absolutely nothing to do with the participation of German soldiers," he told the Die Welt daily, saying the NATO-led force should pull out and hand over peacekeeping duties to the United Nations.
The row recalled a similar phase of hand-wringing last year when the Greens held a special congress to decide if they sould support German participation as part of the IFOR deployment.
The congress said no but the party's members of parliament split on the issue, some voting with the government for deployment while others stuck to the party's pacifist roots.

The party leadership's six-day trip to Bosnia last week has brought the whole issue back out into the open and some members of the delegation have admitted the visit has thrown some of their long-held pacifist views into question.
Officials said the issue could now force its way onto the agenda at a party congress next month.
